sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI  ON THE 4 th OF SEPTEMBER, 2025
MISC. APPEAL No. 3068 of 2017  SATISH  Versus  ARIF AND OTHERS  Appearance:
Shri Surendra Tuteja, learned counsel for the appell  Shri Sudhir Dandwate, learned counsel for the respon  ORDER
The present appeal has been filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 4.8.2017 passed in Claims Case No.1/2015 challenging quantum of compensation.
The liability of Insurance Company is not under dispute.
2. Short facts of the case are that on 26.2.2015 appellant and his wife were returning after attending marriage function.

They were on their way by own motorcycle at around 1.30 in the night, when they reached near Shiv Mandir, respondent No.1 came driving Bolero vehicle No.MP-41-GA-1558 from the side of Dewas in rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of appellant.
Because of which both of them fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
2.1 The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for such injuries.

The claims Tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25170 2 MA-3068-2017 after considering the evidence available on record awarded total compensation of Rs.2,13,000/- to the appellant.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 25%.
In support of his submissions he referred to Ex.P/71 and statement of Doctor (AW-1), wherein he has stated that the appellant suffered injuries in right leg and wrist of right hand.
He, thus prayed that the claims Tribunal should have awarded compensation for sustaining permanent disability to the extent of 25%.
However, the claims Tribunal has awarded a less amount to the appellant.
Apart from this, meager amount has been awarded in conventional heads.
He, thus prays for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance company points out that findings recorded in para 32, 33, of the impugned award in which it has clearly been recorded by the claims Tribunal that fracture of bones are re-united properly as there is no infirmity in the same.

He further points out that in para 34 of the impugned award it has been clearly recorded that the appellant is a salaried employee of the Municipal Corporation, he has not been removed from the job due to the injuries sustained by him, there is no loss of earning capacity as the appellant has received salary as he was receiving before the accident.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.
6.

Considering the fact that irrespective of Ex.P/61 and the statement of Dr.H.S.Rana (AW-2) the fact that the appellant is a salaried employee of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25170 3 MA-3068-2017 Municipal Corporation is not under dispute.
He is still continuing his job is also not under dispute, therefore, he has not suffered any loss of earning.
Any loss of future prospects is also not demonstrated before the claims Tribunal by the appellant.
As such, conclusion of the claims Tribunal in as much the appellant has not suffered any loss of earning due to the injuries are not required to be interfered with.

As regards compensation for injuries sustained by the appellant, it is seen that only an amount of Rs.25,000/- has been awarded for permanent disability suffered to the extent of 25% in the right hand and leg and for other conventional heads like attender, special diet and transportation only a sum of Rs.8,000/- has been awarded.

It cannot be overlooked that though there is no loss of earning capacity because of the permanent disability suffered by the appellant, but naturally there will be loss of amenities and also looking to the meager amount as awarded in conventional heads, this Court thinks it fit to award Rs.60,000/- in lumpsum over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.

The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6%
per annum from the date of filing of claim application till its payment.
7. With the aforesaid, the present Misc.Appeal stands disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE patil Satish vs Arif on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101153591/
